title: Upload size limit is enforced after loading the entire request into memory
reasoning: The route intends to reject files over 10MB, but it calls UploadFile.read() without a limit before checking len(raw_bytes). An authenticated client can submit a much larger multipart file and force the worker to allocate the full payload in memory before the 413 response is produced, making the configured limit ineffective against resource exhaustion.
reproduction: POST /api/config/covers/upload with Content-Type image/png and a payload far larger than 10MB; the handler reads the whole body before returning 413.
recommendation: Read the upload in bounded chunks, stop once max_size + 1 bytes is reached, and return 413 without accumulating more data. Also consider rejecting requests early from Content-Length when present, while keeping the streaming guard as the source of truth.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The discovered manual-cover test only uploads a tiny PNG through the happy path; there is no oversized-upload or memory-boundary test.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test using a fake UploadFile or multipart body over 10MB that asserts the handler returns 413 without calling downstream image normalization and without reading beyond the configured limit.
minimumFixScope: app/api/config.py upload_manual_cover read/limit logic; tests for oversized upload handling.
